title: Go: Distributed Tracing
description: Implement distributed tracing using OpenTelemetry-style spans and context propagation in Go.

steps.title: Create a tracer and root span
steps.description: Create a simulated tracer with a `StartSpan(name)` function that returns a `Span` with `SpanID`, `TraceID`, `StartTime`, and `End()`. Create a root span and print its trace ID using `fmt.Printf("TraceID: %s\n", traceID)`.
hints: Span records name, start time, duration

verification.successMessage: Root span created with trace ID!

steps.title: Nested spans (parent-child)
steps.description: Add a `StartSpan(name, parentSpan)` variant that creates a child span. Create a parent span with 3 child spans (`DBQuery`, `HTTPCall`, `CacheCheck`). Print the span hierarchy using `fmt.Printf("Span: %s (parent: %s)\n", name, parent)`.
hints: Child spans share the same TraceID
SpanContext carries trace and span IDs

verification.failureMessage: Print each span name with its parent span name.

steps.title: Context propagation
steps.description: Implement context propagation by storing the span in a `context.Context`. Create functions `DoRequest(ctx, url)` and `ProcessResponse(ctx, data)` that extract the span from context and create child spans. Print context flow using `fmt.Printf("Propagated: %s -> %s\n", from, to)`.
hints: Use context.WithValue to store the span
Extract span at the start of each function
This simulates how real tracing works across boundaries

verification.failureMessage: Print the span propagation flow between functions.

steps.title: Span attributes and events
steps.description: Add `SetAttribute(key, value)` and `AddEvent(name, attrs)` to the Span. Create a span that records HTTP-like attributes (`http.method=GET`, `http.url=/api/users`) and events (`cache.miss`, `db.query.start`). Print them using `fmt.Printf("Event[%s]: %s\n", spanName, eventName)`.
hints: Attributes are key-value pairs on spans
Use Attributes to query and filter traces later

verification.failureMessage: Print recorded events with their span context.

steps.title: Trace export (simulated)
steps.description: Create an `Exporter` that collects completed spans and outputs them formatted as JSON. Register spans on end, then print the exported trace as JSON using `fmt.Printf("Exported: %s\n", jsonBytes)`. Ensure the JSON contains traceID, spanID, and duration.
hints: JSON output with marshalled Span data

verification.failureMessage: Print the exported JSON trace data.
